_sources.discrepancies: Alaska uses ranked-choice voting (RCV) for general elections for federal and statewide offices since Ballot Measure 2 passed in 2020. NCSL classifies Alaska as non-photo ID (ID requested but not strictly required if voter is known). No separate runoff election exists because RCV functions as an instant-runoff system. 2026-06-10: Primary confirmed as August 18, 2026 and general as November 3, 2026 (elections.alaska.gov / Ballotpedia); registration deadlines follow Alaska's 30-day rule. Early voting begins 15 days before Election Day (Aug 3 primary / Oct 19 general). Corrected an earlier claim that Alaska mails ballots to all registered voters — absentee by-mail requires an application.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting begins 15 days before Election Day (August 3, 2026) at early voting locations; absentee in-person voting is available at Division of Elections regional offices through the day before the election. Absentee by-mail ballots require an application — they are not sent automatically.

Early voting begins 15 days before Election Day (October 19, 2026) at early voting locations and Division of Elections regional offices. RCV ballots used for the general election — rank candidates 1st through 4th.

Early voting begins 15 days before Election Day at early voting locations and Division of Elections regional offices statewide. Absentee by-mail voting requires an application. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting (RCV) for general elections — voters rank up to 4 candidates.

acceptedIds: Alaska driver's license or ID card
If voter is personally known to poll worker, ID may not be required
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Alaska law does not explicitly prohibit phones at polling places, but photographing your ballot or other voters is not permitted. Check with your Division of Elections regional office for local polling place rules.
additionalRules: Alaska uses ranked-choice voting (RCV) in general elections for federal and statewide offices. Voters rank up to 4 candidates. If no candidate receives more than 50% of first-choice votes, lower-ranked votes are redistributed until a winner is determined.
The Alaska primary is a top-four open primary — all candidates appear on one ballot regardless of party, and the top four vote-getters advance to the general election.
Non-photo ID is requested but a voter personally known to the poll worker may vote without presenting ID.

eligibility: Any registered voter may apply for an absentee by-mail ballot — no excuse required
Voters may also vote early/absentee in person at Division of Elections regional offices or vote at their polling place on Election Day
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Absentee by-mail applications must be received by the Division of Elections 10 days before Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, or postmarked by Election Day and received within 10 days
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Return by 8 p.m. Election Day in person, or mail postmarked by Election Day and received within 10 days.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: Alaska uses ranked-choice voting (RCV) in general elections, which functions as an instant-runoff system. There is no separate runoff election.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Alaska uses a top-four nonpartisan primary (Ballot Measure 2, 2020). All registered voters may vote for any candidate regardless of party. The top four advance to the general election, which uses ranked-choice voting.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Alaska utiliza una primaria no partidista de los cuatro primeros (Medida 2, 2020). Cualquier votante registrado puede votar por cualquier candidato sin importar el partido. Los cuatro candidatos con más votos avanzan a las elecciones generales, que utilizan votación por orden de preferencia.
